title: Codex as a Service & the Other Surfaces
description: One Codex engine drives the CLI/TUI, a desktop app, an IDE extension, a remote app-server, and the hosted ChatGPT/GitHub surfaces; mcp-server, app-server, and exec-server expose it as a service.

steps.content: surface 1: argv = [codex]  ->  interactive TUI on the local engine
steps.annotation: The default door is the terminal UI running the agent loop in-process. --no-alt-screen runs it inline, preserving scrollback.

steps.content: surface 2: argv = [codex, app]  ->  launch the Codex desktop app on the same workspace
steps.annotation: codex app opens the desktop app (or its installer) pointed at a workspace path -- a different frontend over the same engine.

steps.content: surface 3: argv = [codex, mcp-server]  ->  serve the engine as MCP tools over stdio
steps.annotation: codex mcp-server turns Codex into a tool another agent can call through the standard protocol.

steps.content: surface 4: argv = [codex, app-server] (experimental)  ->  run the app-server daemon; codex --remote ws://host:port connects a TUI to it
steps.annotation: app-server is experimental: it hosts the engine behind a socket so a thin client (TUI, IDE, remote-control) attaches over --remote with a bearer token.

steps.content: refactor the retry logic (sent from the IDE panel)
steps.annotation: From the user's side the frontend differs; the engine receives the same user turn and starts the same loop.

steps.content: I'll locate the retry path and extract a backoff helper.
steps.annotation: Whichever surface submitted the turn, the loop plans and calls tools identically.
Tool dispatch and sandboxing live in the shared engine, so every frontend inherits the same behavior.
Results stream back to whichever frontend is attached, formatted for that surface.

steps.content: other doors: codex exec-server (experimental standalone service), codex cloud tasks, and the hosted ChatGPT/GitHub integrations
steps.annotation: exec-server, cloud, and the ChatGPT/GitHub surfaces run the same engine hosted elsewhere; only transport and hosting differ.

steps.content: Refactor complete -- same engine, whichever frontend you drove it from.
steps.annotation: The CLI, desktop app, IDE, remote app-server, and hosted surfaces are frontends over one Codex engine.
